name: Question 7
problem:
Let $F(x)=-5x$ for $x\in [0,\pi ).$ Select the correct missing parts in the Fourier sine series of the **odd** $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of the function $F(x)$ below.

$$
f(x)∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,{{field-1}}\cdot {{field-2}}
$$
worked_solution:
For our Fourier sine series, the coefficients are given by

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }f(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=-5x$ for $x\in (0,\pi ).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
{b}_{n}=-\frac{10}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }x\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

We use the integration by parts: 

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⇒\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\, & ⇒\,v=-\frac{1}{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{n} & =-\frac{10}{\pi }(uv\,{|}_{0}^{\pi }-{\int }_{0}^{\pi }v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x) \\  & =-\frac{10}{\pi }(-\frac{1}{n}[x\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)]_{0}^{\pi }+\frac{1}{n}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{10}{n\pi }((\pi \cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )-0\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(0))-\frac{1}{n}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)]_{0}^{\pi }) \\  & =\frac{10}{n\pi }(\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )-\frac{1}{n}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0))) \\  & =\frac{10\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )}{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, since $\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )=(-1)^{n},$ we have

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{10(-1)^{n}}{n}.
$$

Finally, the Fourier sine series is

$$
f(x)∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{10(-1)^{n}}{n}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(nx).
$$

Question 7

Let F(x)=−5x for x∈[0,π). Select the correct missing parts in the Fourier sine series of the odd 2π-periodic extension f(x) of the function F(x) below.
10(1−(−1)n)πn
10(1−(−1)n)πn
10(−1)nn
2(1−(−1)n)πn
2(−1)nn
sin⁡(nx)
cos⁡(nx)
sin⁡(πx)
cos⁡(πx)
sin⁡(nx)
f(x)∼∑n=1∞{(10(1−(−1)n)πn)(S0)}⋅{(cos⁡(nx))(S1)}
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For our Fourier sine series, the coefficients are given by bn=2π∫0πf(x)sin⁡(nx)dx.

In our case, f(x)=−5x for x∈(0,π). So, substituting into the formula, we get bn=−10π∫0πxsin⁡(nx)dx.

We use the integration by parts: u=x⇒u′=1v′=sin⁡(nx)⇒v=−1ncos⁡(nx)

Thus, we obtain bn=−10π(uv|0π−∫0πvu′dx)=−10π(−1n[xcos⁡(nx)]0π+1n∫0πcos⁡(nx)dx)=10nπ((π⋅cos⁡(nπ)−0⋅cos⁡(0))−1n[sin⁡(nx)]0π)=10nπ(πcos⁡(nπ)−1n(sin⁡(nπ)−sin⁡(0)))=10cos⁡(nπ)n.

Therefore, since cos⁡(nπ)=(−1)n, we have bn=10(−1)nn.

Finally, the Fourier sine series is f(x)∼∑n=1∞10(−1)nn⋅sin⁡(nx).
